limbDarkening.source: Neckel H. (2005), Sol. Phys. 229, 13: analytical limb-darkening reference functions for 422-1100 nm, I(mu)/I(1) = sum_k A_k mu^k with A_k = c + l1/lambda + l5/lambda^5 (lambda in micrometres)

corona.source: Baumbach (1937) K+F corona, B(r)/B_sun = scale * sum a_i r^-p_i (r in solar radii, B_sun = mean disk brightness)

granulation.source: Typical solar values: granules ~1,000 km, lifetime ~10 min, white-light rms contrast ~14%; supergranules ~30,000 km (Nordlund, Stein & Asplund 2009, Living Rev. Sol. Phys. 6, 2)

cycle.source: Smoothed monthly sunspot number minima/maxima from SILSO (WDC-SILSO, Royal Observatory of Belgium), cycle shape from Hathaway, Wilson & Reichmann (1994), Sol. Phys. 151, 177: R ~ x^3/(exp(x^2) - c), c = 0.71. Cycle 25 maximum and cycle 26 are estimates; cycles outside the table repeat the generic row every periodYears

butterfly.source: Hathaway D. H. (2011), Sol. Phys. 273, 221: mean emergence latitude ~28 deg * exp(-t / 90 months) from cycle start (Sporer's law); spread and limits approximate

rotation.source: Snodgrass H. B. (1983), ApJ 270, 288: sidereal rotation of small magnetic features omega = A + B sin^2(lat) + C sin^4(lat) (2.902, -0.464, -0.328 urad/s converted to deg/day); frame rate is the IAU WGCCRE W-dot of the Sun (sun.fixed)

spots.source: Typical sunspot-group properties: umbra ~20-30% and penumbra ~75-85% of the quiet-Sun intensity in white light, penumbra/umbra radius ~2.4, groups 50-200 Mm long, Joy's-law tilt ~0.5 x latitude, Gnevyshev-Waldmeier linear area decay over days to weeks; SSN = 10 G + N, so groups on the whole Sun ~ SSN / 7.5 (Solanki 2003, Astron. Astrophys. Rev. 11, 153; van Driel-Gesztelyi & Green 2015, Living Rev. Sol. Phys. 12, 1)

prominences.source: Prominences 10-100 Mm tall, H-alpha (656.3 nm) dominated, brighter than the inner corona in totality (~1e-5 of the disk); quiescent ones live weeks at filament latitudes 15-55 deg (Parenti 2014, Living Rev. Sol. Phys. 11, 1). Brightness factors are approximate

halpha.source: Look of narrowband H-alpha full-disk photos (deep red-orange disk, mild limb darkening); not physical exposure, luminance matched to the white-light disk mean
